issues.body: The shim stores `className` and `classes` independently. In a real DOM, assigning `el.className = "degraded"` or calling `el.setAttribute("class", "degraded")` changes what `el.classList.contains("degraded")` reports, and classList mutations update className. The new self-test exercises only classList directly, so it passes despite this divergence. Current assertions happen to add the `degraded` class through classList, so this does not invalidate this change, but the now-shared shim can still produce a false result for page code that assigns the same class through another standard DOM API.
issues.fix_hint: Back className, setAttribute("class", ...), and classList with one shared class set (or add synchronized getters/setters), then extend the probe to assign a class through className or setAttribute and observe it through classList, plus the reverse direction.
issues.title: Shared shim does not synchronize className and classList

verdict.summary: The refactor correctly consolidates the three Node page harnesses behind one builder, preserves each harness's exports and body, and adds a non-vacuous executed check of the shim's class, attribute, child-replacement, recursive-degradation, ID-memoization, namespace, text, and app-loading behavior. The existing page assertions continue to exercise their real renderers, and the exact-count check catches reintroduction of the former literal prelude. I found no blocker or major correctness, security, or fail-closed regression. One minor fidelity gap remains in the shared DOM model: className/setAttribute("class") and classList do not share state as they do in a browser.
